name: beautiful-extension
description: Write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Chrome extensions on Manifest V3 + TypeScript: three skills distilled from Chrome's MV3 documentation, the Web Store policies, the extension security guidance, and the facta extension handbook, plus a drop-in eslint config.

interface.longDescription:
Three skills for Chrome extension developers on Manifest V3, distilled from Chrome's MV3 documentation, the Web Store program policies, the extension security guidance, and the facta extension handbook.

extension-best-practices guides new extension code: the event-driven service worker, top-level listener registration, typed storage with migrations, sender-validated messaging, least-privilege permissions, a strict CSP, content-script boundaries, the SDK in the worker, and the unbreakable layer contract.

extension-review reviews a worker, content script, popup, manifest, message contract, or diff and returns a prioritized report. Architecture and sender validation rank above everything. Every finding cites a file and line, the rule it breaks, and the smallest fix.

extension-port ports MV2 background pages, Firefox/Edge extensions, or a web app to MV3 with the same behavior. It ports the original tests first and writes a PORTING.md that lists every deliberate difference.

The skills contain instructions and reference text only. They make no network calls and collect no data. When a Node.js toolchain is available, the skills run tsc, eslint, and vitest on your project; without one, they work from the code alone. A drop-in eslint config is available in the GitHub repository.
capabilities: Port MV2 or web code to MV3 with the same behavior
defaultPrompt: Review this extension manifest and list what to fix first
Port this MV2 background page to a service worker
Write a sender-validated message handler for this feature

publication.release_notes: Initial release: three MV3 skills, the layer and sender-validation contract, and a proven eslint config.
